WHY_SIX_TRANSFER_STATES_NOT_MORE: There are three recipient choices and, under single-unit complementary compensation, exactly two distinct donor choices for each recipient. Hence 3*2=6 ordered transfer vectors e_i-e_j. Without the minimality gate, each recipient has infinitely many integer compensation decompositions and more than six states.
WHY_TWO_BRANCHES_NOT_THREE_OR_INFINITE: With unit recipient +1 and sheet conservation, transverse total is -1. Under the discrete minimal completed-state gate, exactly one of the two transverse coordinates supplies the single -1 and the other supplies 0, giving two ordered decompositions. Remove the minimality/discrete endpoint gate and integer solutions are (t,-1-t), t in Z; remove sheet coupling and four endpoint combinations survive; allow non-unit positive recipient increments and a third r=2 branch appears.
